subject: Upload a data file across all sessions

messages.author: c16f1b13c9ab3235
messages.subject: Upload a data file across all sessions
parts:
Hi all Shiny users,

I am trying to implement a shiny app that deals with uploaded dataset (a data.frame for example), there is nice tutorial on the webpage, http://jcheng5.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#uploads, and I am fine with reproducing the example codes. But according to my understanding, this example shows a way reading the .csv file in a per-session manner. This is inapplicable in my case, I need to upload it once and use this file across all sessions. I think I should use "reactive" rather than "render...", so I modified the code as following:

library(shiny)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  dataset <- reactive({
    inFile <- input$file1
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
    
    read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
  })
  
  output$contents <- renderTable({
    dataset
  })
})

But it gave me error message:

Error in UseMethod("xtable") : 
  no applicable method for 'xtable' applied to an object of class "c('refMethodDef', 'function', 'SuperClassMethod', 'OptionalFunction', 'PossibleMethod')"

I also tried with other methods I think makes sense but didn't work :( 
I will appreciate for you help. Thanks in advance.

Best regards,

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Upload a data file across all sessions
parts:
You could put code like this before your call to shinyServer, i.e. at the top of server.R (see this for why it goes there):

sharedData <- reactiveValues()

Inside your shinyServer function, have this:

observe({
  if (is.null(input$file1))
    return()
  sharedData$dataset <- read.csv(input$file1$datapath, ...)
})

output$contents <- renderTable({
  sharedData$dataset
})

The "observe" means that the enclosed chunk of code will be re-executed as necessary (in this case, whenever input$file1 changes). When it executes and input$file1 is present, it will read the file and put it in the sharedData reactive values holder with the name "dataset". Then you can refer to sharedData$dataset in all of your other render calls, reactives, etc.

Note that while I believe this will work, Shiny is currently not particularly well optimized for this use case. For example, if your observe code also includes input$header, input$sep, input$quote then when a user changes one of those it will cause their session to replace the sharedData$dataset value even if theirs was not the most recent file to be uploaded. You may be able to work around this with judicious use of the "isolate" function. I definitely recommend reading all three of the "Understanding Reactivity" chapters in the tutorial.
